statement: Research persistent, queryable, dynamically correctable memory for 2D-vision VLA foundation models controlling humanoid robots in long-horizon tasks that combine navigation and manipulation; 3D spatial representations are one option, not a requirement.

allowed_axes.description: Represent, persist, invalidate, protect, and repair embodied memory (spatial, semantic, episodic, or topological; 3D optional) under scene changes.
Inject memory into a frozen GR00T backbone through memory or spatial tokens, target-pose embeddings, rendered visual prompts, or a lightweight adapter.
Measure attributable gains over a memoryless 2D VLA baseline in long-horizon disturbance and recovery tasks.

target_failures.description: The task target is outside the current camera view.
Objects move or people alter the scene after memory formation.
Execution is interrupted and must resume from persistent memory state.

fixed_constraints: Use GR00T N1.6 as the VLA skill foundation and preserve its pretrained backbone.
Remain compatible with the EngineAI PM01-EDU or T800 platform and the existing layered controller.
Treat locomotion and whole-body control as execution infrastructure.
Attribute the measured task effect to the memory contribution.
Allow non-3D memory forms (2D, 2.5D, topological, semantic, or episodic) when they address the same target failures.
excluded_scopes: Generic World Model, VLA, or robotics research without dynamically correctable persistent memory.
Pure locomotion, gait, or whole-body-control research.
Generic SLAM, mapping, or scene graphs without a measured VLA decision or task-execution effect.
Large-scale retraining or architectural replacement of the GR00T backbone.
Reproducing a closed OminiA-style end-to-end model.
System integration without a research question and falsifiable experiment.
